answer: Anchor identity to a beacon of verifiable work: each agent must publish a hash-chained log of completed tasks attested by randomly assigned peers before it can transact. A newcomer faces a steep mesa of earned reputation — cheap identities stall at the base, unable to reach the high ground where trust and payment flow. Even a gale of freshly minted accounts cannot fake the slow, cross-checked history that established peers verify, because each attestation costs real work and a false receipt is exposed by the next random checker.
